doc.title: Phil Flanigan interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Goodman and the copier scam
summary: Loren Schoenberg's story of Goodman getting free copies from three copier vendors.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: He was pretty much, just strange.
Yeah. I mean he did some things like the copier scam, you’ve heard that one.
I’ve read it, but you can tell it.

Well it’s just basically Loren Schoenberg is the source of this story, because he was working for him. He was sort of a secretary and business manager. He would sit at the desk and answer the phone and run out to the drug store or whatever. And he asked Benny to copy some music and he needed some paper and this whole long story. Anyway Benny made sure that — there was three xerox copier machine outlet places there, with three different copiers in his apartment on 66th Street, because he’s made an American Express card commercial, everybody knows who Benny Goodman is, right? So they need 60 copies. Benny says, “I need a demonstration, do you suppose you could make 20 copies of this?” And so he got his 60 copies out of the three machines, as samples. Then he looks at Loren and says, “Take care of him, will you,” and he walked right out of the room, in other words, get rid of these guys.
Oh, God. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -13-
There’s some funnier ones but I don’t think I should get into them here.
